uncited: *   **Section Memory:** An external memory block acting as a large FIFO.
It stores intermediate values (such as accumulated color and opacity, or gradient data) that would normally be passed between pipeline stages.
**Partitioning:** The volume dataset is partitioned into sections.
*   Let $S$ be the set of sections, where $S = \{s_1, s_2, ..., s_n\}$.
*   Let $I_{right}$ be the intermediate values generated by the right-hand pipeline.
*   Let $I_{left}$ be the intermediate values consumed by the left-hand pipeline.
Handles loading volume data into memory; Sectioning operates on already loaded data, partitioning it for processing [Link](2045-volumeloader.md).
Uses hardware buffers for streaming; Sectioning uses external memory for FIFO recirculation [Link](2119-hardware-assisted-volume-streaming.md).
Determines streaming intervals based on bandwidth; Sectioning determines section boundaries based on memory limits [Link](3128-bandwidth-based-streaming-interval-calculation.md).
Divides space for parallel processing; Sectioning divides space for memory management within a single pass [Link](3862-chunk-based-spatial-partitioning.md).
Distributes work across nodes; Sectioning manages memory within a single node's pipeline [Link](5624-distributed-computing-and-load-balancing.md).
Uses MapReduce for parallel rendering; Sectioning is a hardware pipeline optimization [Link](5963-mapreduce-based-volume-rendering.md).
Loads bricks from disk; Sectioning manages intermediate values in external memory during rendering [Link](6288-out-of-core-brick-based-volume-rendering.md).

*   The condition for correctness is: $I_{left}(s_i) = I_{right}(s_{i-1})$ for $i > 1$, where $I_{right}(s_{i-1})$ is stored in Section Memory and retrieved as $I_{left}(s_i)$ [S1, unofficial].

The evidence explicitly states that 'Section Memory acts as a big, external FIFO capable of holding values that need to be recirculated in the x-direction' and that 'Exactly the same values are written to, then read from, Section Memory as would have been passed to the next pipeline.' It further clarifies that 'the left-hand pipeline either reads values from Section Memory (at the beginning of a section) or accepts them from the right-hand pipeline.' This confirms that intermediate values (which correspond to the right-side state of the previous section, $I_{right}(s_{i-1})$) are stored in Section Memory and retrieved by the left-hand pipeline (as $I_{left}(s_i)$) for the next section, ensuring correctness without approximation.

Unlike [Hardware-Assisted Volume Streaming](2119-hardware-assisted-volume-streaming.md) which relies on hardware buffers for streaming, or [Chunk-based spatial partitioning](3862-chunk-based-spatial-partitioning.md) which divides space for load balancing, Sectioning specifically manages the recirculation of data within a single rendering pass to maintain exact numerical precision without approximation [S1, unofficial].

The evidence explicitly states that Sectioning partitions the volume dataset to manage on-chip memory limits by off-loading intermediate values to external memory (Section Memory). It confirms that this memory acts as an external FIFO for recirculating data in the x-direction. Crucially, the text asserts that 'Exactly the same values are written to, then read from, Section Memory as would have been passed to the next pipeline,' ensuring that 'no approximation is made.' This directly supports the claim that Sectioning manages recirculation within a rendering pass to maintain exact numerical precision without approximation.
